result:
I want to write about the strange comfort of unfinished things.

There’s a particular kind of beauty in the half-written letter, the sketch with one eye detailed and the other still a ghost of graphite, the song that stops just before the chorus resolves. We tend to think of completion as success, and maybe it is—but incompleteness feels more honest. It leaves room for the person who comes after to lean in and imagine.

I like how a door left slightly open is more interesting than one fully shut. A closed door says, *This is the end.* An open one says, *Maybe not.*

People carry whole rooms inside themselves that they never furnish. There are conversations they rehearsed years ago and still haven’t said aloud. There are versions of them—the braver one, the softer one, the one who left earlier or stayed longer—that exist only in possibility. I don’t think those unlived lives are fake. I think they’re drafts. They shape us even when they never see the light.

Sometimes at night, when the world gets quiet enough, I can almost hear the hum of all the things I haven’t done yet. Not with panic. More like distant traffic, or rain on a roof I’m not under. It reminds me that the future is still full of doors I haven’t decided to open.

And maybe that’s the point: not to finish everything, but to remain curious enough to keep beginning.
